topic: Circuit Breakers Fail Without Gateway Concurrency Caps
postText:
When an external lab integration stalled during peak hours in our healthcare facility, our gateway did not protect us. The downstream circuit breaker tripped exactly as configured. Yet, within ninety seconds, our entire gateway collapsed. Workstations across triage and admissions threw 504 Gateway Timeouts.

The culprit? Gateway thread pool starvation.

A circuit breaker evaluates failure thresholds over sliding time windows. While error rates climb toward trip thresholds, hundreds of slow requests keep worker threads and TCP sockets parked. Inflight requests exhaust the gateway worker pool. Unrelated critical routes—patient vitals, pharmacy queues, triage routing—starve and die because the edge layer has no spare execution threads.

Fix cascading failure by pairing breakers with upstream control:

1. Bulkhead Route Isolation: Isolate gateway connection and worker pools per upstream service. A saturated lab route must never consume thread budgets assigned to patient admission routes.
2. Adaptive Edge Rate Limiting: Couple distributed token buckets with downstream health telemetry. Throttle inbound volume before worker queues back up.
3. Zero-Delay Fallbacks: Return synthetic cached snapshots or immediate 429/503 responses directly at the ingress proxy. Never hold TCP connections waiting for remote timeouts.

Resilience means protecting the edge from burning its own sockets while waiting for dying dependencies.

How do you partition gateway worker pools to stop one degrading backend from taking down your entire ingress tier?
